sources.researchNote: BnF gives 1896–1985 in its heading, with 10 February 1896 and 15 August 1885 in its coded dates, the second evidently a keying error for 1985. It describes him as a screenwriter, film dialogue writer and song lyricist, Legrand being a pseudonym of Henri André Steigelmann. The Library of Congress name authority n2007044635 and GND 1105687570 both give 1896–1986. Consulted through the BnF SRU service.

media.title: Henri-André Legrand on the set of Procès au Vatican, 1952
media.description: Portrait detail of the screenwriter and lyricist Henri-André Legrand from a photograph published in La Cinématographie française on 23 February 1952. The printed caption names André Haguet, director, first and André Legrand, dialogue writer for Procès au Vatican, second; Legrand is therefore the man on the right.
media.altText: Halftone press portrait of Henri-André Legrand in a dark suit and tie, looking slightly upward while seated on a film set.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The portrait is a press photograph printed in La Cinématographie française on 23 February 1952 without a photographer’s credit, and therefore treated as an anonymous work, for which the French term of seventy years from publication ran out at the end of 2022. It was protected in France on 1 January 1996 and the URAA restored United States copyright for ninety-five years from publication, to the end of 2047. The Media History Digital Library permits use of material in its collection in teaching, research and publications, but that permission covers the digitised volume it supplies and not a third party’s copyright in the photograph. The local copy is reduced to 493 × 800 px.
